headline: Eastern Connecticut outpaces the Little East
dek: Eastern Connecticut finished with thirteen wins against three losses and two draws, scoring 49 goals — more than any other program in the conference — while conceding fifteen. That return set the pace across the full schedule and left the rest of the Little East chasing from behind.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Scoring in the Little East is top-heavy rather than evenly spread: Eastern Connecticut's 49 goals exceed the combined totals of Western Connecticut and UMass Boston, leaving the rest of the conference clustered well below the leader.

wire.line: Outside the conference, Little East sides posted 35 wins, twelve draws, and 34 losses, scoring 113 goals and conceding 124.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: UMass Boston goalkeeper Janiya Morales Matier recorded 107 saves and allowed fifteen goals, posting an 0.877 save percentage.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Plymouth State finished the season with ten wins, seven losses, and zero draws.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Western Connecticut drew seven matches alongside six wins and five losses, finishing with more draws than any other program in the conference.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: VTSU Castleton conceded 47 goals while scoring fourteen, giving up more goals than any other program in the Little East.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Southern Maine spread its offense across at least thirteen different goal scorers over the season.

last_match.line: Eastern Connecticut had won every home match all season before this defeat ended its unbeaten run since September.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
